newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed somewhat higher on Friday and dealers said market players were nervous ahead of the second round of the French elections on Sunday.
"If it means another victory for the French socialist party this will probably press the French bond market lower and other Eurepean markets will follow the trend," said one dealer.
"We only need some reassuring words from the Socialist party about the EMU if they win the elections on Sunday," said another dealer, adding this would calm the market.
Participants have expressed fear over a delay in building the EMU if the Socialist party wins the second round.
Dealers said they expected prices of Dutch bonds to drop a little early next week, with yields edging up.
The new GDP data from the United States did not bring much movement in the bond market.
The U.S. first quarter GDP rose by 5.8 percent, the strongest rise since the fourth quarter in 1987.
"The GDP figure was slightly better than expected," said one dealer as analysts had forecast a rise of 6.0 percent.
One dealer said investors might slowly turn away from the stock market and invest more in bonds.
"Investors taking their profit in the share market could choose bonds as interest rates are seen stable," he said.
